request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The steward's dashboard counts are now over the sheet and all its descendants.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The steward's dashboard now counts over the sheet and all its descendants, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

The only file I changed is `src/main/frontend/features/dashboard/dashboard.slot.tsx`; I didn't need any server or stored-data changes. It now gets the sheet and every sheet below it using the same lookup the consolidated panel uses (`useFamily`). It counts PENDING, REVIEW and overdue claims on each of those sheets, then adds the counts up. Each sheet's overdue count uses that sheet's own today and late-charge settings. A sheet with no children still shows just its own counts.

The counts only show if you are a steward on the sheet you have loaded. Being a steward on a child sheet doesn't matter; that sheet's claims are counted either way.
